the leachate quality at Tre Monti landfill is stable over time, the lagoon treatment facility removes most of the leachate pollutants, and the soil layer underneath the lagoon offers an effective barrier against migration.

the leachate produced in the Tre Monti landfill site is characterized by a high variability of the concentration of most pollutants, that the pre-treatment of the leachate in a non-aerated pond system allows the reduction of the pollutant concentration in the leachate, but does not allow the complete removal of all contaminants, and that the subsoil clay layer acts as a barrier to the vertical migration of contaminants.

a proper management of landfill leachates, including pre-treatment and monitoring, can be a useful tool for reducing the impact of landfills on the environment and for minimizing the risk of contamination.

, for an active landfill site, the monitoring of leachates and sub-superfical water quality, as well as the analysis of soil samples, are key tools for assessing the potential of the site for contamination of surface and ground waters and for the planning of the future management of the landfill.
